channel.title: Los Angeles Review of Books – Reviews
channel.description: Book reviews from the Los Angeles Review of Books.

item.title: Murky Effects
item.description: A novel of desire and domestic disorder amid a disintegrating literary establishment.

item.title: Female Power Versus Toxic Masculinity
item.description: The three newly translated novellas in Belgian author Jacqueline Harpman’s ‘We Were Forbidden’ display a storytelling skill that seems magically effortless.

item.title: Why Didn’t India Build Its Own Silicon Valley?
item.description: Dwaipayan Banerjee’s new book investigates India’s role in the history of 20th-century tech development, and what caused it always to seem a step behind the West.

item.title: Sowing the Seeds of Apology
item.description: Roland Orzabal of Tears for Fears makes amends in his new ‘astrological memoir.’

item.title: Bending the Arc of History
item.description: A new biography of Howard Zinn functions less as a detailed portrait of a man than as an inspirational manual for contemporary endurance.

item.title: California Sons: Miriam Pawel’s “The Browns of California”
item.description: Jake Wertz reviews “The Browns of California,” a four-generation biography of the Brown family and a portrait of the state they shaped.

item.title: The Uncommitted Man
item.description: A new translation of Ivan Turgenev’s 1867 novel ‘Smoke’ explores the main concerns of the author’s life.

item.title: Why Did the Roman Empire Last So Long?
item.description: Edward J. Watts’s history of the long Roman Empire is a traditional, top-down political narrative.

item.title: The Filmography That Launched a Thousand Ships
item.description: Decentering Homer and reflecting on the self-referential nature of Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey.’

item.title: Anything Could Become a Battleground
item.description: Isaac Butler’s new book mixes history and personal testimony to examine the ‘culture wars’ that shaped the 1980s—conflicts that differed in striking ways from the ones we’re witnessing today.

item.title: The Fate of China’s Muslims
item.description: Two recent books track the history of China’s Muslim minority during a period of suspicion and suppression.

item.title: Anarcho-Thumbelina
item.description: Romanian author Oana Aristide’s new novel is an entertaining fable of serial murder, killer bears, and revolution.

item.title: Drowning Airplanes Give You So Much More
item.description: On Megan Mi-Ai Lee at Tiffany’s in Los Angeles.

item.title: The Animator’s New Groove
item.description: A personal history of animation’s reconquest of Hollywood.
